title: Dynamic Topology State & Governed Spatial Operations
objective: Implement live anomalous topology state and governed spatial operations over the sealed MSLR-01 profile/runtime core: typed connect/disconnect/redirect/permute/wrap/fold/nest/phase/collapse/stabilize/sever operations through Action/Event/GPR; preview/dry-run/revalidation; Event trace/replay; inverse/compensation/recovery classifications; stale/concurrent mutation rejection; and the owner-approved architecture amendment for explicit edge/region identifications, quotient topology, authored orientation-reversing connections, local walker/frame state, and bounded lazy neighborhood expansion without rewriting canonical World/Location identity.
acceptance: Live topology state stores MSLR-owned anomalous relation state without rewriting reusable World/Reality/Scene/Location definitions.
Typed topology operations route through Action/Event/GPR owner execution and honor permission/version checks before commit.
Edge/region identifications and quotient topology are explicit authored topology semantics rather than inferred portal shortcuts.
Orientation-reversing authored connections update explicit local walker/frame state while preserving canonical location identity.
Unbounded or procedurally addressed substrates evaluate bounded local neighborhoods lazily and never require exhaustive world enumeration.
Preview/dry-run is noncanonical and commit revalidates stale owner/profile/runtime versions.
Declared-deterministic topology state replays from accepted profile versions plus immutable Event history.
Reversal uses owner-defined inverse, compensation or recovery semantics and never deletes committed history.
Stale or concurrent mutation attempts fail deterministically before canonical commit.
Blocking topology-operation workflows remain semantic/nonvisual, keyboard-capable, provider-off and paid-cloud independent.
boundaries: MSLR-01 and upstream completed programs remain sealed.
World/Reality/Scene/Location owners retain canonical identity and base semantic-location truth.
Transition/Portal/Access owners retain traversal and portal authorization; quotient identification is not silently converted into portal state.
GPR/Action/Event retain generic execution, Event history and replay authority.
MCS retains projection/presentation authority; a projection never becomes topology truth.
MSLR local frame/walker state is MSLR runtime state and never replaces Character, Location or World identity.
Lazy neighborhood expansion is bounded computation over an accepted law/substrate and does not imply exhaustive generation or a duplicate World ledger.
MSLR-04 and later MSLR tranches remain unauthorized until canonical MSLR-03 closeout.
External hyperbolic/HyperRogue research remains clean-room architecture guidance only; no protected implementation or expression is copied.
next_action: Await the next owner Continue. That command may governed-start only MSLR-03.
